blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In real life, profit and cash diverge for predictable reasons. A company growing fast often shows strong profits but weak cash flow, because it is investing in inventory, hiring people and extending credit to new clients before the revenue catches up.

At Czarnikow, the treasury team watches this gap carefully. They forecast cash needs weeks in advance, manage credit lines with banks and make sure the company always has enough liquidity to meet its obligations. A profitable quarter means nothing if you cannot pay your suppliers on time.

Understanding why profit and cash diverge is a key skill for any business professional. It helps you ask better questions, spot risks earlier and make decisions that protect both the top line and the bank balance.

items.q: According to the text, why does a fast-growing company often show weak cash flow?
options: Because its profits are usually overstated
Because its suppliers refuse to extend credit
Because it invests in inventory and credit before the revenue arrives
Because it stops forecasting cash needs
items.why: "it is investing in inventory, hiring people and extending credit… before the revenue catches up."

items.q: What does the treasury team at Czarnikow do to manage the gap?
options: It delays payments to suppliers
It reduces the company's profit targets
It stops extending credit to new clients
It forecasts cash needs and manages credit lines with banks
items.why: "They forecast cash needs weeks in advance, manage credit lines with banks…"

items.q: What does "A profitable quarter means nothing if you cannot pay your suppliers on time" suggest?
options: Suppliers should always be paid before employees
Quarterly reports are unnecessary
Liquidity matters as much as reported profit
Profit is easy to fake in a quarterly report
items.why: Inferência: o autor coloca a liquidez no mesmo patamar do lucro — sem caixa, o lucro no papel não sustenta a empresa.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Growth can consume cash even when profits look healthy
A strong profit figure guarantees a company has cash to spend
Understanding cash flow helps you spot risks earlier
A profit-cash gap can usually be explained by clear causes
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que lucro forte NÃO garante caixa disponível.

items.q: The phrase "protect both the top line and the bank balance" implies that a good professional…
options: leaves cash decisions entirely to the banks
focuses only on increasing revenue
cares about revenue and liquidity at the same time
avoids taking on any new clients
items.why: Inferência: "top line" (receita) e "bank balance" (caixa) juntos — os dois importam.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver falando com a equipe comercial. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before anyone gets frustrated, let me be clear: I'm proud of this quarter. You closed strong deals and the profit line looks excellent. So the question I keep hearing is fair — if we made all that profit, where is the cash bonus?

Here's the honest answer. The profit is real, but it hasn't turned into cash yet. To win those big accounts, we agreed longer payment terms — sixty, even ninety days. And to deliver, we bought inventory up front. So the money is sitting in working capital, not in the bank.

Think about it this way. If we had won the same deals on our old thirty-day terms, we would have collected the cash months earlier, and there probably would have been a bonus this quarter. That's the third conditional at work — different terms, different outcome.

So this isn't bad news and nobody was dishonest. The cash is coming; it's just arriving later than the profit. Keep selling, but from now on, flag the payment terms early so treasury can plan the liquidity around them.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Oliver's overall attitude towards the team's quarter?
options: He is proud of the results despite the cash issue
He thinks the profit figure is exaggerated
He blames the team for the missing bonus
He is disappointed with the deals they closed
items.why: "I'm proud of this quarter. You closed strong deals and the profit line looks excellent."

items.q: Why hasn't the profit turned into a cash bonus?
options: Longer payment terms and up-front inventory tied the money up
The banks refused to release the credit lines
The company recorded the profit incorrectly
The team spent the bonus on new hires
items.why: "we agreed longer payment terms… we bought inventory up front. So the money is sitting in working capital."

items.q: According to Oliver, what would have happened on the old thirty-day terms?
options: The inventory would have cost more
The profit would have been higher
The deals would have been lost to competitors
The cash would have arrived earlier and a bonus was likely
items.why: "we would have collected the cash months earlier, and there probably would have been a bonus."

items.q: What can we infer about why Oliver mentions "nobody was dishonest"?
options: Someone had already been accused of fraud
He wants to reassure a team that might feel cheated of a bonus
He suspects the treasury team of hiding money
The auditors found an error in the accounts
items.why: Inferência: ele antecipa a frustração — quer deixar claro que o dinheiro só está atrasado, ninguém agiu de má-fé.

items.q: What does Oliver want the team to do differently from now on?
options: Reduce the amount of inventory they buy
Close fewer but larger deals
Flag payment terms early so treasury can plan liquidity
Stop offering longer payment terms altogether
items.why: "flag the payment terms early so treasury can plan the liquidity around them."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Profit and cash often diverge during rapid growth." To diverge means to…
options: be reported twice
grow at exactly the same rate
move apart or differ
cancel each other out
items.why: Diverge = divergir, seguir caminhos diferentes.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The cash isn't missing — it's tied up in ___, mostly inventory and unpaid invoices."
options: dividends
net profit
working capital
payment terms
items.why: Working capital = capital de giro: onde o dinheiro fica preso (estoque, contas a receber).

items.q: "We agreed ninety-day payment terms to win the account." Payment terms are…
options: the total value of the contract
the discount given for early payment
the agreed period the client has to pay
the interest charged by the bank
items.why: Payment terms = prazos de pagamento acordados com o cliente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "That figure was a ___ — it won't repeat next quarter, so don't build the forecast on it."
options: credit line
dividend
top line
one-off sale
items.why: One-off sale = venda pontual, que não se repete.

items.q: "The board approved a dividend only after checking liquidity." A dividend is…
options: a payment of profit to shareholders
a loan taken from a bank
a tax on company earnings
a discount offered to clients
items.why: Dividend = dividendo: parte do lucro distribuída aos acionistas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the dividend." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
postpone indefinitely
question in public
calculate roughly
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Longer payment terms tie up a lot of cash." To tie up cash means to…
options: make it immediately available
convert it into profit
lock it so it can't be used freely
lose it permanently
items.why: Tie up = deixar preso/imobilizado, sem poder usar livremente.

items.q: "Treasury asked us to flag long terms early." To flag something means to…
options: point it out for attention
cancel it quietly
approve it automatically
keep it confidential
items.why: Flag = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para algo com antecedência.

items.q: "Give the team a moment before you dive into the numbers." To dive into means to…
options: summarise briefly
avoid discussing
start examining in detail
delegate to someone else
items.why: Dive into = mergulhar, começar a analisar a fundo.

items.q: "None of this will move the needle on liquidity this month." This means it will…
options: not make a noticeable difference
cause serious resistance
cost more than expected
take longer to measure
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
